title: Broadcast guarantees and delivery order
summary: Separate receiving from delivering, then compare FIFO, causal, total, and FIFO-total broadcast guarantees.
objectives: Distinguish a received message from a delivered message
State the guarantee and scope of four broadcast models
Explain why buffering is needed for stronger ordering

sourceLens.whyExaminable: The lecture asks which delivery guarantee preserves which dependency. The common trap is treating FIFO, causal, and total order as interchangeable.

sections.title: Receive is not deliver
sections.body: A broadcast algorithm may receive a message from the network and hold it in a buffer before delivering it to the application. The delivery step is where the chosen ordering guarantee is enforced.

sections.title: Four guarantees, four scopes
sections.body: FIFO preserves the order of messages broadcast by one process. Causal broadcast preserves happens-before between broadcasts. Total order makes every process deliver all messages in the same order. FIFO-total order adds per-sender FIFO to a common global order.

math.name: Causal broadcast guarantee
math.purpose: Check whether delivery respects a causal dependency between broadcasts.
math.explanation: If the broadcast of $m_1$ happens before the broadcast of $m_2$, every process must deliver $m_1$ first.

examples.title: Choose the weakest sufficient guarantee
steps: If only one sender's channel order matters, FIFO is sufficient.
If a dependency crosses processes, use causal ordering.
If every process must see one identical sequence, use total order.
Expect buffering and metadata when the guarantee is stronger.
examples.answer: The correct guarantee is determined by the invariant the application must preserve, not by choosing the strongest label automatically.

contrastDrills.prompt: Messages from different senders are causally related. Which guarantee captures that dependency?
contrastDrills.explanation: FIFO is channel-local; causal broadcast follows happens-before across processes.
contrastDrills.misconception: Identify whether the dependency crosses a sender channel.

contrastDrills.prompt: Which guarantee requires all processes to deliver messages in exactly the same order?
contrastDrills.explanation: Total order imposes one common delivery sequence; causal order only constrains causally related messages.
contrastDrills.misconception: Causal order does not order concurrent messages globally.

criticalQuestions.prompt: Why can a received message be unsafe to deliver immediately?
criticalQuestions.angle: Ask which earlier message or ordering condition may still be missing.
criticalQuestions.modelAnswer: A later message may arrive before a causally earlier dependency. Buffering lets the implementation wait until the selected delivery guarantee is safe.

criticalQuestions.prompt: What distinction separates causal order from total order when two broadcasts are concurrent?
criticalQuestions.angle: Check whether the guarantee constrains only happens-before or imposes one common sequence for every process.
criticalQuestions.modelAnswer: Causal order constrains messages related by happens-before but may leave concurrent broadcasts in different orders. Total order requires every process to deliver all broadcasts in the same order, including concurrent ones.
